cards.text: Zechariah, a prophet, is in the middle of a run of visions from the LORD. Then the prophet says, 'Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.' Friend, that's the look of a man about to tell you your new oven won't fit through the door.

cards.question: Zechariah asks the man with the measuring line where he's going. What is he heading out to measure?

cards.text: Then the angel who's been talking with Zechariah heads out, and another angel comes forward to meet him. Two angels, one message, and this one can't wait.

cards.question: The second angel says to run and tell that young man about Jerusalem. What kind of city will Jerusalem be?

answers.text: A city high on a hill

cards.question: Jerusalem will have no walls because its enemies will keep tearing them down.

cards.text: No walls, because the city's too FULL of people and livestock. That's a cookie box so packed the lid just gives up and sits on top like a hat.

cards.question: With no walls around Jerusalem, the LORD says a wall of fire will surround it. Who is that wall of fire?
The LORD also says He will be the glory within Jerusalem.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out to His people who are far from home. He says He's the one who scattered them, like the four winds of heaven.

cards.question: After scattering His people, the LORD tells them to stay where they are in the land of the north.
The LORD calls Zion to get up and escape. Who have they been living with?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks of a 'Me' that His Glory has sent against the nations that plundered His people. Uh oh, somebody's about to get a visit.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says whoever touches His people touches the apple of His eye. What does that show about His people?

answers.text: They are a burden to Him

cards.text: Touch His people and you're poking Him right in the eye, and friend, NOBODY stays calm when you go for the eye. Then the one speaking says He will surely wave His hand over those nations.

cards.question: A hand is waved over the nations that plundered God's people. What happens to those nations?

answers.text: They become plunder for their own servants
They are scattered to the four winds

cards.question: When this happens, God's people will know that the LORD of Hosts sent the one who is speaking.

cards.text: Now the mood FLIPS, and the LORD tells the Daughter of Zion to shout for joy and be glad. Friend, after all that scattering talk, that's the kind of news you read twice just to make sure your eyes still work.

cards.question: Why does the LORD tell the Daughter of Zion to shout for joy?

answers.text: He is coming to dwell among them
Their new walls are finally finished
Their enemies are begging for peace

cards.question: On that day, the LORD says, many ___ will join themselves to Him and become His people.
The LORD will take possession of ___ as His portion in the Holy Land, and He will once again choose ___.
In the last line, the LORD has roused Himself from His holy dwelling. So what are all people told to do before Him?

cards.text: And that's where this vision lands. But hold on, friend, Zechariah's not done seeing things yet.

findings.problem: The joke is aimed at God. 'Touch His people and you're poking Him right in the eye, and friend, NOBODY stays calm when you go for the eye' makes the punchline God losing His temper. It treats the LORD's protection of His people like someone flinching and snapping when poked.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: 'Then the LORD of Hosts speaks of a 'Me' that His Glory has sent' is hard to follow, and the nested quote marks make it worse. A baker can't tell that 'Me' is the one speaking these words. The card can leave open who that speaker is and still say plainly that the speaker says His Glory has sent Him against the nations.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card is verse 12 almost word for word with two blanks, and no story card sets it up. Judah has not been mentioned anywhere before, so picking Judah over Samaria is wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. The two right answers can also be argued in either order, since Jerusalem is in Judah. A baker could say the LORD takes Jerusalem as His portion and chooses Judah.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Multiple choice is 5 of the 9 choice cards in stop 2, against 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. Both stops also repeat the same pairing: a multiple choice card followed by an easy true or false follow-up (stop 1 cards 7-8, stop 2 cards 7-8).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
